organism.common_name: Miocene Stickleback Chronospecies III (Pelvic Loss, T=+22 kyr)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Gasterosteus doryssus_late (27 µm, detail scale)
phenomenon_scale.not_the_sibling_scale: Slot 1209 uses 1.7 mm (6_organ_mm). This slot does not copy those parameters.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = 0.5 * (tr_k + sqrt(tr_k^2 - 4 det_k)), tr_k = tr J - k^2 (D_u + D_v)
equations.selected_mode: k_m = argmax sigma(k), lambda_m = 2 pi / k_m
equations.boundary_condition: periodic on a 1D ring (Fourier mode of the Turing analysis)
equations.ocellus: far-field spiral R(rho) sin(k_m * s + theta + phase), the ocellus topology selected when the late-stage flank patch is only a few wavelengths across

what_changes_at_this_scale: At 27 µm and 9.99 Ma the pelvic-loss chronospecies shortens activator range relative to doryssus_mid (33.62 µm spots around vestigial-spine ossicles) and has not yet reached the marine plate-row spacing (21.48 µm). Loss of the pelvic girdle opens one nearly isotropic flank patch a few wavelengths wide, so the same Turing band is expressed as a single ocellus rather than as extended stripes.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 dispersion relation and diffusion-driven instability
Kondo & Miura 2010: pigment patterns as reaction-diffusion wavelengths
Hunt, Bell & Travis 2008: Truckee Formation stickleback lineage moves toward a new pelvic optimum
reconstructed_in_script: Schnakenberg parameters and r = 25 chosen so the fastest mode is 27.07 µm at 9.99 Ma
Du scaled as lambda_m^2 across mid / late / marine
Hagan-style far-field spiral used as the late ocellus render
transfer_boundary: 27 µm is a detail-scale tier assignment, not a caliper measurement on a Truckee fossil
Gallery plate is an illustrated ocellus card with a 100 µm bar, not a Miocene thin section
does_not_claim: Does not claim fossil melanophores were measured at 27 µm
Does not claim the gallery JPEG is a photograph of specimen UCMP material
Does not reuse the 1.7 mm organ-scale parameters of slot 1209

sources.citation: Turing AM (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37-72.
Hunt G, Bell MA, Travis MP (2008) Evolution toward a new adaptive optimum: phenotypic evolution in a fossil stickleback lineage. Evolution 62:700-710.
Kondo S, Miura T (2010) Reaction-diffusion model as a framework for understanding biological pattern formation. Science 329:1616-1620.
